title: reading-notes-llm-inference-daniel-brooks
content:
Quick reading notes + TODOs -- trying to collect practical takeaways for Redwood serving runtime and the Dedicated/Private product paths. Mostly scattershot; jotting ideas and references to revisit.

High-level themes (why this matters for Redwood):
- Latency vs throughput tradeoffs: many papers optimize throughput (large batch, kernel fusion) but production SLOs often bound tail latency. Need strategies to adapt kernels and batching based on SLOs and request distribution.
- Quantization + accuracy: 4-bit / mixed-precision can dramatically reduce memory and improve throughput, but we need robust per-model quant recipes and quick fallbacks when quality regressions show up in evals.
- KV/prefix caching: large win for chat-like workloads with repetition and long contexts; eviction policies + sharding cache across GPUs matter.
- Kernel-level optimizations (FlashAttention, fused MLPs): critical for high perf on A100/H100 and newer CPUs. Evaluate cost-benefit across our fleet.

Papers/blogs to re-read / main notes:
- "FlashAttention" (Dao et al.) -- arXiv:2207.14235
  - Core idea: compute attention with IO-aware algorithms to avoid materializing big attention matrices; reduces memory and increases speed for long sequences.
  - Prod takeaway: implement low-overhead hotpath that detects long-seq requests and switches to Flash-friendly kernels. Must measure switch cost.
  - Link: https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.14235

- "GPTQ / quantization for LLMs" (various repos: github GPTQ-for-LLaMA, bitsandbytes)
  - 4-bit PTQ & GPTQ provide near-floating accuracy with huge memory wins. But per-layer calibration and handling folded layers is finicky.
  - Ops: add a quantization validation pipeline: run our small eval suite (safety, hallucination, instruction-following) before shipping a quantized variant. Tag model in catalog with quant profile.
  - Risk: some prompt templates (few-shot) degrade faster. Add synthetic prompt sets to evals.

- "FlashAttention 2 / optimized kernels" + vendor libs (NVIDIA/Triton, FasterTransformer)
  - Keep a matrix of kernel performance by model size, batch size, seq len, and GPU type. Use this to inform kernel selection in serving runtime.
  - Action: build microbench harness for common model shapes we serve; automated nightly runs to update profiles.

- "KV cache sharding and prefix caching" blog notes (various)
  - Cache hit model: store per-session KV in memory with TTL; use best-effort eviction. For Dedicated, allow customers to tune TTL vs memory.
  - For Private deployments, provide guidance for shared-cache sizing and sharding across devices to avoid hotspots.

- "Routing & model variants" (our internal thesis)
  - Route by latency target: fast small quantized model for low-latency, high-quality bigger model as fallback. Maintain consistent output via distillation/temperature calibration.
  - Keep deterministic subset tests so A/B regressions are catchable.

Practical experiments to run (short-term):
1) Microbench: run FlashAttention vs baseline on H100/A100 for seq lenses [64,128,512,1024] for 7B/13B/70B; measure p50/p95/p99 and memory footprint. (Owner: Owen)
2) Quantized eval harness: take 3 top models we serve, create 4-bit GPTQ variants, run eval suite (our user prompts + open benchmarks) and produce a pass/fail for deployment. (Owner: Maya)
3) KV cache simulation: synthetic workload generator to measure hit rate and tail latencies under varying TTL and sharding policies. (Owner: me)

Notes / rough heuristics observed from reading:
- Small batch sizes + long seq length often favor attention optimizations more than kernel-level MLP fusions.
- Mixed precision (bf16 + int8 weights) can reduce memory but watch accumulation precision for very deep layers.
- Caching effectiveness depends heavily on conversational UI: if users send multi-turn messages with many system prompts, hit rate drops; but for short assistant-only turns, hit rate is excellent.

Unresolved questions / open design decisions:
- How to version quantized model variants in the catalog so users can pin and roll back cleanly? Need catalog metadata fields: quant_profile_id, calibration_dataset_id, eval_snapshot_id.
- Fallback policies: when quantized variant fails eval or degrades on live metrics, automatic fallback to float variant must be instant -- implement circuit-breaker + warm-up.
- Cost accounting: how to attribute savings from batching/caching to customer invoices accurately? We need token-level meter that knows whether token was served from cache or deduplicated by batching.

Links / bookmarks (to revisit):
- FlashAttention: https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.14235
- FlashAttention PyTorch impl: https://github.com/pytorch/flash-attention
- GPTQ repo: https://github.com/IST-DASLab/gptq
- NVIDIA FasterTransformer: https://github.com/NVIDIA/
